body: Or it might work better if all the voting rights are held by the bond holders and once an incremental target is met a portion of your bond token is converted to the NFT backed token. So you might mint fractional shares for your NFTs, sell half of them and hold the other half to pay the bond holders at your milestones rather than after 10 years. That uses the benefits of both mechanisms.

It's pretty exciting once it all makes sense - and here I was thinking NFTs were just fools gold.
Another thought I had is to issue more tokens incrementally as milestones are acheived. If this issuance is controlled by a 3rd party like an oracle controlled by an environmental group then the voters have a greater incentive to elect the right people into the council as they are not only working to increase the value of their tokens but to gain more of them on a regular basis. Like a positive feedback loop reinforcing the goals of the DAO. It would have to be often enough and small enough not to dilute the value of your tokens too much like once a month or every quarter. Or it might have more impact on electing if you do it less often, might be worth experimenting to see which timeframe works best. Sorry if that's already in the works as well but I had to mention it.

Sorry I haven't posted for a while. I've had less time than I thought, but I have been doing some research and think I'm on to something that might work.

I've been trying to come up with more of an equity based solution to acheive the same thing described earlier and just came across NFT backed tokens. This got me thinking, what if the NFTs didn't just represent artwork but the goals and values of the DAO collecting and distributing funds. So in our case, an NFT collection might be made of GIFs representing climate goals like pre-industrial levels of carbon or having no mercury in the ocean - one NFT for each measurable metric. People interested in these goals can bring their crypto in exchange for a fractionalized share of these NFTs. The DAO will spend that crypto on real world projects realising these goals.

There's nothing radically new here except the NFTs are representing a potential future rather than the least risky investment they can think of. I guess it reintroduces purpose to your investment rather than being locked into making decisions based solely on financial gain. Although if all the hype surrounding NFTs is accurate then financial gain will follow as a result anyway.

In theory, the most growth potential for the value of these NFT collections is when there is a great need for early investment so they would be better at getting started with eco solutions than they would be at maintaining optimal conditions later on. I think this is what we need right now though.

Thanks for the update, I actually went back and read up on _war bonds _which is where you said your initial inspiration came from...

> A war bond is a debt security issued by a government to finance military operations during times of war or conflict. Because war bonds offered a rate of return below the market rate, investment was achieved by making emotional appeals to patriotic citizens to lend the government money.

Tweaking the [key takeaways from the post](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/w/warbonds.asp) to suit this idea...

- A climate bond is an initiative by a decentralised collective to _coordinate_ and fund green projects and spending by issuing debt for the global public to purchase.
- The global public may buy these bonds out of a feeling of duty, or other emotional appeal.
- Although climate bonds do not typically pay interest, they are sold at a discount that mature to face value, typically after a period of 10 to 30 years.


Your follow on point:

> just came across NFT backed tokens. 
> This got me thinking, what if the NFTs didn't just represent artwork but the goals and values of the DAO collecting and distributing funds. So in our case, an NFT collection might be made of GIFs representing climate goals like pre-industrial levels of carbon or having no mercury in the ocean - one NFT for each measurable metric. 
> People interested in these goals can bring their crypto in exchange for a fractionalized share of these NFTs. The DAO will spend that crypto on real world projects realising these goals. 

This is exactly where we're heading with new projects, except rather than this design being used for _money in _from investors, it's executed on _money out _for projects - for example the green projects you are targeting here.

So for example, you are a renewable energy project at high risk R&D stage that has technology that could benefit all countries equally and such should be in the public domain, rather than any one country who would naturally exploit the innovation for national aims ahead of public goods. 

That project submits a funding proposal to the DAO (Edgeware/Kabocha etc) and assigns NFTs representing the mission / vision / goals and even utility / permissions / licences in return. 

Over time these assigned assets become more valuable owing to the ideas and narratives becoming more established, which in turn builds underlying collateral to the community treasury and since these assets are  collectively owned, governed and assigned, other DAO members are encouraged to build on these assets.

Based on this initial phase we could then spin out a chain dedicated to this model and fund more projects with similar climate aims. 

That chain would have exactly the same model as before - capturing assigned NFTs in its reserves in return for funding innovative teams and projects.

As you've noted above, we could then create a security based on fractionalising the collateral and offer bonds to the public and to institutional investors which drives the flywheel further, and offers a path to fund even more projects.

Well the EDG treasury would be perfect to fund small R&D projects - if you'd be interested we could try and scope that out to try and put some meat on the bones? 

You don't have to have all the answers - it's most important to have a keen interest, a curious nature and a willingness to try and figure stuff out. 

I'd suggest an initial grant would enable you to spend a little time researching the area. Tbh, it might even just begin with a research report or analysis...

Regen Network looks pretty cool, do you think they would be interested in this idea?
